question: Matrices $X$ and $Y$ of order $2\times2$ satisfy $$X+Y=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\5&2\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$2X-Y=\begin{bmatrix}6&4\\1&7\end{bmatrix}.$$ Using matrix operations and equality of corresponding entries, determine $X$ and $Y$ and verify that the obtained matrices satisfy both the given equations.
explanation:
Formation of the Required Matrices

Let $$M=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\5&2\end{bmatrix},\quad N=\begin{bmatrix}6&4\\1&7\end{bmatrix}$$ The given equations are $X+Y=M$ and $2X-Y=N$. Adding these matrix equations, $$3X=M+N$$ Therefore, $$3X=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\5&2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}6&4\\1&7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}9&3\\6&9\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$X=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}9&3\\6&9\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\2&3\end{bmatrix}$$ From $X+Y=M$, $$Y=M-X=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\5&2\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\2&3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&-2\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}$$

Verification

Now, $$X+Y=\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\2&3\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0&-2\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\5&2\end{bmatrix}$$ Also, $$2X-Y=\begin{bmatrix}6&2\\4&6\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}0&-2\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}6&4\\1&7\end{bmatrix}$$ Since the corresponding elements agree in both equations, the required matrices are $$X=\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\2&3\end{bmatrix},\quad Y=\begin{bmatrix}0&-2\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}$$.
